entities.name: Tiridates II of Armenia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Tiridates II of Armenia (flourished 2nd half of 2nd century CE), known as Khosrov in Armenian sources, was an Arsacid Prince and Roman Client King of Armenia.

Tiridates II was the son and heir of Khosrov I, king of Armenia, and ascended to the throne following his father's death in 228 CE. He played a crucial role in maintaining Armenia's independence from the Roman Empire, navigating a complex web of alliances and rivalries with neighboring kingdoms.

Tiridates II's reign was marked by significant military campaigns, including the Battle of Samosata in 242 CE, where he clashed with the Roman Emperor Gordian III. Despite ultimately being defeated, Tiridates II's bravery and strategic prowess earned him a reputation as one of the greatest kings of the Arsacid dynasty.

His legacy continued to shape Armenian politics and culture for centuries to come, with Tiridates II being remembered as a champion of Armenian identity and sovereignty.

"The glory of Armenia is the glory of the world," Tiridates II once declared, highlighting his unwavering commitment to his people and his kingdom.
